reference_class.outside_reasoning: Treaties governing vital shared resources like rivers have a high historical rate of renewal because the alternative (legal vacuum on water sharing) is exceptionally costly for both downstream and upstream parties. Applying the base rate of 85% adjusted by a general diplomatic friction factor yields a moderate-high probability.

Deve Gowda and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, and the historic 2015 Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) ratified under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This current episode differs crucially from 1996 in that bilateral ties are no longer shaped by the post-Cold War search for foundational confidence-building measures, but rather by high-stakes transactional pragmatism, as evidenced by simultaneous logistical continuity like RITES dispatching passenger coaches to Bangladesh Railway despite recent political transitions in Dhaka. Unlike the 2015 LBA episode—which required overcoming decades of domestic constitutional hurdles through absolute political capital—the present context features an urgent functional imperative over transboundary water management that supersedes interim domestic turbulence, removing the paralysis that typically plagues bilateral disputes.
